interest: Index of Japanese army factionalism, 1930–36, to the February 26 Incident.
overview: This file consists of nine pages of the Department of State's official List of Papers (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.20 (Military Affairs - Japan / Army of Japan), indexing entries numbered 62 through 156 dating from April 1930 to March 1936. The docket sheets record incoming diplomatic despatches, telegrams, military attaché reports, intelligence memoranda, and cross-reference notes that document the Japanese Army's organization, rearmament programs, and political ascendancy. Key topics include early army reform and modernization efforts, the 1931-1932 Manchurian Incident and subsequent military operations across North China, urban air-defense preparations in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, the distribution of military propaganda pamphlets, and severe internal factional discord highlighted by the removal of General Masaki, the August 1935 assassination of Military Affairs Bureau chief Major General Tetsuzan Nagata, and the February 26, 1936 military coup d'état attempt.

subfiles.about: Department of State docket list indexing papers and cross-references filed under decimal file 894.20 concerning the Japanese Army and military affairs from 1930 to 1936.
subfiles.summary: This document comprises nine sheets of the official Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) cataloguing decimal file 894.20 (Military Affairs - Japan / Army of Japan) across sub-numbers 62 through 156 between April 1930 and March 1936. It records and summarizes diplomatic despatches, telegrams, military attaché reports, and cross-reference sheets tracking the Japanese Army's expansion, strategic preparations, and growing political power. Major episodes indexed include army modernization, the Manchurian crisis, municipal air-defense measures, internal factional conflict culminating in the assassination of Major General Tetsuzan Nagata by Lieutenant Colonel Aizawa, and the Tokyo military insurrection of February 26, 1936.
